extraction.name: PIQA: Physical Interaction: Question Answering
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for evaluating and studying physical commonsense understanding in natural language models, framed as multiple-choice question answering with goal and solution pairs.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by prompting crowd annotators with links to instructables.com from six categories (costume, outside, craft, home, food, and workshop). Annotators were asked to extract or be inspired to construct two component tasks: formulating a goal, providing a correct solution, and providing an invalid permutation or trick that sounds reasonable but is subtly incorrect.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Instructions from instructables.com across six categories: costume, outside, craft, home, food, and workshop.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was filtered using the AFLite algorithm to remove annotation artifacts and stylistic biases using BERT-Large embeddings and linear classifier ensembles. Text was tokenized using Spacy, and for model experiments, examples were truncated at 150 tokens. The train, development, and test splits were automatically produced by AFLite.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd annotators completed a qualification HIT requiring >80% accuracy in identifying well-formed (goal, solution) pairs. In the main HIT, annotators formulated a physical goal, a valid solution, and an incorrect trick solution. Data was collected in batches of several thousand triples and validated by other annotators for correctness. Users with low agreement were de-qualified, and examples with low agreement were removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Validation HITs evaluated data correctness. Examples with low annotator agreement were removed from the dataset, which frequently filtered out examples requiring expert-level domain knowledge rather than commonsense. Human performance was calculated via majority vote among qualified annotators.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were paid an average of >$15/hr based on self-reporting on turkerview.com and timing calculations. Annotators were qualified based on achieving >80% (or ~90% for human performance evaluation) on a qualification HIT.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Reporting biasswamps unconstrained goal-solution prompts because humans rarely mention obvious or atypical physical properties and lean towards prototypical solutions. Annotation artifacts and stylistic biases that artificially inflate model performance were systematically addressed using AFLite.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: AFLite filtering and validation removed examples requiring expert domain knowledge; some apparent validation errors were actually correct but required external web search verification.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, training, validation, and testing of natural language understanding models on physical commonsense reasoning.
